claims.statement: Indulging in idealized positive fantasies about a desired result (living it as already achieved, without obstacles) lowers the energy, effort and achievement that follow, compared with questioning, negative or neutral thoughts.
claims.population: adults and students pursuing a personal goal
claims.exposure: idealized positive fantasies about the desired result, indulged as if already achieved
claims.comparison: fantasies that question that future, negative or neutral thoughts about it

claims.statement: Mentally rehearsing the steps toward a goal (process simulation) improves effort and performance more than picturing the desired result (outcome simulation).
claims.population: students and adults preparing a task, an exam or a health goal
claims.exposure: mental rehearsal of the steps toward the goal (process simulation)
claims.outcome: effort, persistence and performance (study, grades, weight, tasks)

claims.statement: Contrasting the wished-for result with the obstacles in the way, then planning if-then responses (MCII, WOOP), helps people reach their goals more than only dreaming of the result or doing nothing.
claims.population: adults and students with a personal goal
claims.exposure: mental contrasting with if-then plans (MCII, WOOP)
claims.comparison: only dreaming of the result (wishes, sham WOOP), or a control activity

claims.statement: Embracing the path itself, by enjoying it or by reading its discomfort as a sign of progress, makes people engage and persist more at their goals than focusing only on the later result.
claims.population: adults and students pursuing health, study or personal-growth goals
claims.exposure: enjoyment of the activity, intrinsic motivation, or seeking discomfort as a sign of growth
claims.comparison: focus on later rewards, extrinsic motivation or incentives, standard instructions

notFound: no independent replication (outside Oettingen's laboratory) of the effect of positive fantasies on energy or achievement, and no meta-analysis of positive fantasies against expectations (both agents, three bases)
no head-to-head meta-analysis of process against outcome simulation: Cole 2021 compares each with control; in its 4 studies with both arms, process does no better (its data file, read by the reviser)
no replication of Pham & Taylor 1999, nor of Woolley & Fishbach 2022 (seeking discomfort); no multi-lab replication of MCII/WOOP; no MCII meta-analysis after 2021

no Egyptian sample for anything in this episode; Arab samples: Alghazo 2020 (269 Saudi women students, c2), Armitage 2017 (216 adults in Kuwait, questionnaires in Arabic, nationality not reported; if-then plans alone, c3), Alshammari 2026 (218 Saudi students of Ha'il, 56% men, cross-sectional, c4); none for positive fantasies, the MCII package or an experiment on c4
Hofstede scores of Arab countries not read; Kizilcec 2017 found an effect only in the English-speaking cluster (an African-Islamic cluster was tested)
Lambert 2022 (expatriate pupils in Dubai): a multi-component wellbeing program that includes mental contrasting, no goal outcome, no control group in the abstract: not kept

not kept, plans alone rather than the MCII package (they would nuance c3 as Armitage 2017 does): Gollwitzer & Sheeran 2006 (no abstract), Sheeran, Listrom & Gollwitzer 2024, Breitwieser & Reinelt 2026, Cooke 2022, Pakpour 2016 (Iran), Melum 2026, Silva 2018

not kept: Prokopowicz & Byrka 2021 (process against outcome not tested as such in the abstract, overall p = .073); Riddell 2023 (MCII null for 111 cyclists, same direction as Kudrna and Kędra); Sezer 2025 (no control group)

not kept: Al-Hoorie 2018 and Kim 2026 (the L2 ideal self: correlations, a measure confounded with self-confidence, i.e. expectations); Frikha 2025 (Saudi, enjoyment and physical activity, cross-sectional); David 2024 (effort feels aversive: the book's premise, not a tested claim); Houser-Marko 2008, Freund 2015 (indirect)
found and not kept by the writer: Meslot 2016 (two RCTs, null), Vasquez & Buehler 2007, Renner 2019, Kappes, Oettingen & Mayer 2011 EJSP (same laboratory)

full texts not read: Woolley 2022 (closed; its OSF protocols and preregistrations read by the second blind review), Marszał-Wiśniewska 2014 (closed), Oettingen 2001 and 2002, Pham 1999, Cross 2019, Cerasoli 2014; Woolley 2025 and Wittleder 2025 (KOPS) were read by the second blind review
Europe PMC answered 503 to two queries on 2026-11-23 (culture or moderator; publication bias): run again on OpenAlex; its full text of Kizilcec 2017 answered 500 (read on the PMC page)

no independent replication of the experiments on c4 (Woolley 2016, 2022, 2025 study 4: one laboratory, one session or 24 h); no trial of MCII against only dreaming outside the creators' laboratory (second blind review, 2026-11-26)

found.note: offered against c1 and c2: g = .23 for imagined success is a subgroup of an omnibus test that is not significant (p = .16), against no simulation, not against questioning thoughts: a nuance of both, not a contradiction

preregistered, 134 adults in Australia: thinking of the outcome raised reported motivation right after, the steps lowered perceived control; no effort or performance measured and the process arm did not take (dz = 0.07): a nuance of c1 and c2

Al-Hoorie 2018 (and Kim 2026, 10.3390/educsci16060892): the ideal L2 self goes with more intended effort; correlations, the measure confounded with self-confidence, i.e. the expectations c1 sets apart from fantasies: not taken
no independent replication of positive fantasies (Kappes 2011, Oettingen 2002) in the works citing them: every retest comes from the same laboratory; c1 stays low and supports only its narrow reading
for c2: the process group lost more weight at five weeks, study 1 only (about 10 women per group, weight measure not described); study 2 shows no process advantage: added, c2 stays mixed
for c2: more perseverance after process simulation, on easy mazes one leaves at will, alternating assignment, skewed data: added with a downgrade for risk of bias
Prokopowicz & Byrka 2021: process against outcome not tested as such in the abstract, overall p = .073: not taken

the largest randomized head-to-head (269 Saudi women students): no difference at the midterm or in engagement; outcome ahead early in the term, process later: contradicts c2, which becomes very low after the second review

the card: 87% of its 15,907 participants are in one online study whose effect held only in English-speaking countries; 13 of 21 articles by MCII's creators; Egger t = 5.46, 0.242 after trim-and-fill: no participant count on the card
preregistered, 12,879 students of individualist countries: MCII did not raise course completion, its interval excludes the original gains: c3 mixed, and the nuance said
no effect in collectivist or « balanced » countries, an effect only in the English-speaking cluster; MC and II alone changed nothing
independent preregistered cluster trial, 225 employees whose control states a wish: no added progress at four weeks; imprecise (28 of 60 workplaces, 29% lost)
two small online trials in Poland, both null, powered for a medium effect only
Riddell 2023: MCII did not support goal attainment for 111 cyclists; same direction as Kudrna and Kędra, not added
Cooke 2022: if-then plans on alcohol, null at university and online; plans alone, not the MCII package: not added
for c3, the exact comparator: WOOP against a sham WOOP that dreams twice, fewer heavy drinking days at 1 and 2 months; a feasibility pilot (86 randomized, unequal loss), creators co-authors
if-then plans alone in Kuwait (216 adults, questionnaires in Arabic, nationality not reported): more weight lost at 6 months, d = .38; no mental contrasting: a nuance of c3, refused for the screen
the direct test of the book's idea: seeking discomfort as a sign of growth raised engagement, in the same session, one laboratory: c4 rewritten to test it
intrinsic motivation predicts adherence over a year (U.S.) and a month (China), associations; study 4 causal over 24 h, d = .21: c4 stays low, never « for years »
218 Saudi students: intrinsic motivation goes with reported effort (r = .88), not with grades, cross-sectional: a nuance of c4, not support
David 2024: mental effort goes with negative affect in 29 countries: the book's premise (effort costs), not a tested claim: not added
Pakpour 2016, Iran: if-then plans raised toothbrushing in adolescents; plans alone, not MCII: not added

counterEvidence.conclusion: ⚖️ holds, ✅ and ❌ excluded. Taken: c1 narrowed to the idealized dream (Cole, Hallford: nuances); c3 mixed (Kizilcec 2020, Kudrna, Kędra against; bias and allegiance in Wang); c4 rewritten on Woolley 2022; c2 very low, so the verdict is very low; the participant count left the card; the nuance said moved from c1 to c3. Not taken: splitting c3, a fifth claim.
